answer.reason: The mutant only changes the order of keys in the serialized JSON. Loading the file gives back the same system prompt, history and version, so round-trip preservation and version rejection are unaffected. No requirement asks for a canonical byte layout.
sources: Saving and loading a session shall preserve its system prompt, conversation history, generated text, metadata, and supported embedded media across the serialized representation.
Unsupported serialization versions raise SessionSerializationError instead of loading incompatible state.

review.reason: Changing the sort order of keys in the JSON serialization string does not affect the logical data structure, so the system prompt, history, and media are completely preserved during round-trips.
sources: Requirement REQ_SESSION_PERSISTENCE (Session persistence round-trips state): Saving and loading a session shall preserve its system prompt, conversation history, generated text, metadata, and supported embedded media across the serialized representation.
